lines.t: [Intro - fingerpicked guitar, quiet room]
I keep reading what You did...
Then looking at my life
Like You became somebody else.
Four hungry men outside the gate,
No welcome left, no food to take.
A starving city at their backs,
An enemy beyond the tracks.
They walked toward the Syrian tents,
Expecting death with every step.
But God had made an army flee—
And left a feast where fear should be.
Bread for hands the city shunned,
Before the morning work was done.
The men nobody would let near
Brought news the starving longed to hear.
And I'm staring at an empty shelf,
As though You never fed the weak.
All the history I believe—
Why is it so hard to trust this week?
If He did it then,
Can He not now?
Has His arm grown short?
Has His love run out?
When the numbers say it's over,
When there's nothing I can do,
Let the weakness in my body
Find its strength in what is true.
My promises must be kept.
Then let my heart remember
What my fear forgets.
A widow with a debt to pay,
Two sons they meant to take away.
One little jar, an emptied room,
Borrowed vessels waiting too.
She shut the door and tipped the oil;
It filled the emptiness before her.
One more vessel, then one more—
Still the little jar could pour.
Until no empty vessel stood,
The oil kept coming, more than enough.
And what she thought was all she had
Became provision in His hand.
I keep counting what is missing.
I keep measuring my lack.
But a little in Your keeping
Isn't little in my hands.
If He did it then,
Can He not now?
Has His arm grown short?
Has His love run out?
When the numbers say it's over,
When there's nothing I can do,
Let the weakness in my body
Find its strength in what is true.
My promises must be kept.
Then let my heart remember
What my fear forgets.
Assyria stood outside the walls,
With threats enough to shake them all.
The king spread out the words he'd read
Before the LORD, and bowed his head.
No boast could force the Holy One.
No army told Him what to do.
One angel went into the night;
The morning showed the threat was through.
And I let a sentence break my sleep.
I let tomorrow make me crawl.
But the One who heard Jerusalem
Has not become less Lord of all.
[Instrumental - thunderous melodic guitar, then sudden quiet]
Abraham with silver hair,
Sarah long past hope to bear.
A promise older than their strength,
Years that seemed to stretch its end.
Then Isaac breathing in her arms,
Laughter where the sorrow was.
Not because the years were kind—
Because the LORD fulfilled His word in time.
Oh, the tenderness of that:
A child against an aged chest.
The answer had a living face.
The waiting hadn't made Him less.
And suddenly I'm not demanding
That You make my wishes true.
I'm ashamed of how I've measured
All Your faithfulness by You
Doing what I thought was needed
On the day I thought was best.
You have never owed my panic
An explanation for Your rest.
The sea was not too deep to open.
The stone was not too sealed to move.
And the grave could not keep YahuShua—
What can make Your word untrue?
Not every prison opened early.
Not every faithful servant spared.
Yet no suffering made You faithless;
No dark valley meant You weren't there.
I don't need to write the ending.
I don't need to name the hour.
I need trust enough to follow
When I cannot see Your power.
If He did it then,
Can He not now?
Has His arm grown short?
Has His love run out?
YahuShua-YAHUWAH,
You have not forgotten how
To sustain the weak and weary,
To bring the proud heart bowing down.
I have read of all Your wonders—
Now Your faithfulness breaks mine:
All my little walls of keeping
You outside the fear inside.
[All instruments stop]
My promises must be kept.
Then I can take the next step.
I can take the next step.
Bread where they expected dying!
Oil where the last drop fell!
Laughter in the tent of waiting!
Jerusalem delivered still!
Not a story left behind us.
Not a God whose strength is spent.
Let the weary lift their faces—
He is faithful to His word!
The trouble isn't over.
But I'm not facing it alone.
If You did it then...
You have not changed.
Let me trust what You have spoken.
Let me rise...
And walk again.
